extracted.intended_audience: mariners, vessel owners/operators, local stakeholders, small businesses, and members of the public interested in submitting comments to the Coast Guard rulemaking (Regulations.gov users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and the proposed regulatory text for a Coast Guard supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking modifying drawbridge operating regulations for the Atlantic Beach Bridge; includes instructions and standards for public participation and regulatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments close / Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments and relate material must reach the Coast Guard on or before March 22, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments identified by docket number USCG-2022-0854 through the Federal Decision Making Portal at https://www.regulations.gov. See the “Public Participation and Request for Comments” portion of the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section for instructions on submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit a comment, please include the docket number for this rulemaking, indicate the specific section of this document to which each comment applies, and provide a reason for each suggestion or recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps the agency consider and respond to comments effectively; follow the step-by-step instructions on Regulations.gov (search USCG-2022-0854 → select document → click Comment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and alternate instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments identified by docket number USCG-2022-0854 through the Federal Decision Making Portal at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your material cannot be submitted using https://www.regulations.gov, contact the person in the FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT section for alternate instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment posting, redaction, and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard will only post comments that address the topic of the proposed rule; it may choose not to post off-topic, inappropriate, or duplicate comments. Posted comments will include any personal information you have provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous comments and privacy notice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments we post to https://www.regulations.gov will include any personal information you have provided. For more about privacy and submissions, see DHS's eRulemaking System of Records notice (85 FR 14226, March 11, 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entities / Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Flexibility Act requires Federal agencies to consider the potential impact of regulations on small entities; the Coast Guard certifies under 5 U.S.C. 605(b) that this proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you think your business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction qualifies as a small entity and that this rulemaking would have a significant economic impact on it, submit a comment explaining why you think it qualifies and how and to what degree this rulemaking would economically affect it. Contact the person listed in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for assistance; the Coast Guard will not retaliate against small entities that question or complain about this proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Planning and Review / EO 12866
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Orders 12866 and 13563 direct agencies to assess the costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives and, if regulation is necessary, to select regulatory approaches that maximize net benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This SNPRM has not been designated a 'significant regulatory action' under EO 12866 and has not been reviewed by OMB. The determination is based on the ability that vessels can still transit the bridge given advanced notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would call for no new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism and Indian tribal governments analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule has implications for federalism under Executive Order 13132 if it has a substantial direct effect on the States or on the distribution of power; this proposed rule has been analyzed under that Order and determined consistent with federalism principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposed rule does not have tribal implications under EO13175 because it would not have a substantial direct effect on Indian tribes; if you believe otherwise, contact the person listed in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act requires agencies to assess effects of discretionary regulatory actions, particularly those causing expenditures of $100,000,000 or more in any one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though this proposed rule will not result in such an expenditure, the Coast Guard discusses effects of the proposed rule elsewhere in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental review / NEPA categorical exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coast Guard has determined that this action is one of a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment and is categorically excluded under paragraph L49.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither a Record of Environmental Consideration nor a Memorandum for the Record are required for this rulemaking. The Coast Guard seeks any comments or information that may lead to the discovery of a significant environmental impact from this proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest activities coordination (First Amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coast Guard respects the First Amendment rights of protesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protesters are asked to contact the person listed in FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT to coordinate protest activities so that messages can be received without jeopardizing safety or security of people, places, or vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation importance and how comments influence rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coast Guard views public participation as essential to effective rulemaking and will consider all comments and material received during the comment period; your comment can help shape the outcome of this rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include docket number, specify sections, provide reasons for recommendations, and submit through Regulations.gov or contact FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT for alternate submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and docket access instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: To view documents mentioned in this proposed rule as being available in the docket, find the docket on Regulations.gov and select 'Supporting & Related Material' in the Document Type column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments will also be placed in the online docket and can be viewed by following instructions on the Regulations.gov Frequently Asked Questions web page. Signing up for email alerts notifies you when comments are posted, when a final rule is published, and of any posting or updates to the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed regulatory text — §117.799(e)(1): Oct 1–May 14 schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: From October 1 through May 14 the draw shall open on signal from 8 a.m. to midnight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the proposed operating schedule for the Atlantic Beach Bridge to be codified in 33 CFR 117.799(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed regulatory text — §117.799(e)(2): Midnight–8 a.m. notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: From midnight to 8 a.m. year-round, the draw shall open on signal if at least eight (8) hours of notice is given by calling the Bridge Tower at 516-239-1821.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amends existing regulation to require advance notice for openings during midnight–8 a.m. hours and adds the Bridge Tower phone number for mariners to contact when requesting a bridge opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed regulatory text — §117.799(e)(3): May 15–Sep 30 peak-season schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: From May 15 through September 30, the bridge will open on signal except from 4 p.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays and from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Saturdays, Sundays, Memorial Day, Independence Day, and Labor Day when the bridge will open on the hour and half-hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies reduced frequency (on-the-hour and half-hour openings) during identified peak periods and holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridge owner request and revision rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nassau County Bridge Authority requested decreasing the number of openings on signal from October through May and later requested adding a bridge tower call number and removing outdated language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Coast Guard states the change is expected to better serve the needs of the community while continuing to meet the reasonable needs of navigation; background notes reduced commercial activity and two public meetings with no public attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related documents and comment status
rubrics_metrics.description: Related docket documents include earlier NPRM and final rule listings; public comments: 3 comments have been received at Regulations.gov; Comments are no longer being accepted. See DATES for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FederalRegister.gov page displays related documents and indicates whether comments are still being accepted; use provided links to view the official PDF and public inspection versions.
